items.title: WHILE YOU SLEPT, ONE MODEL SPENT 10 DAYS BREAKING LINUX AND FOUND 948 DOORS TO ROOT.
items.summary:
WHILE YOU SLEPT, ONE MODEL SPENT 10 DAYS BREAKING LINUX AND FOUND 948 DOORS TO ROOT.

not a hacker group. not a state. a pipeline of OpenAI agents running on $1.2M of API

that kernel runs your server, your Android and the cloud. and it wrote a patch for every door    
           
GPT-6 Cyber is a separate model trained to find bugs and write working exploits. i went through the 27-min report, here's the line stage by stage

▹ what runs under the hood

1. SCOUT agents: 5,034 audit targets · 2.8M lines · 7% of the kernel · $3,426

2. ANALYST agents: 2,308 candidate findings in 12h · $316,549

3. TRIAGE agents: PoC in a KASAN VM, retry until it crashes · 1,724 reproduced in 30h · 74.7% hit rate · only 3.1% wrong analysis

4. EXPLOITDEV agents: SMEP · SMAP · KASLR on, stock distro · 1,169 working root shells · 948 distinct bugs · $1,279 per bug

5. PATCH agents: a patch for every bug · 304 critical sent to maintainers first · humans review before anything ships

6. same harness, new brain: GPT-5.6 Sol in july → 166 · GPT-6 Cyber in october → 948 · 5.7x

SCOUT → ANALYST → TRIAGE → SCREEN → EXPLOITDEV → PATCH → HUMAN

firefox: 81 new high-severity bugs. Mozilla already shipping fixes (MFSA 2026-118). Mozilla and Palo Alto Networks are on Cyber already

cost: $1.2M in API for one run. at Pwn2Own / TyphoonPWN prices those 948 exploits are worth $18.9M–$66.3M

access: no public release. GPT-6 Cyber goes to approved orgs via Daybreak Red, behind an IP allowlist. defenders get GPT-6 Astra via Daybreak Blue. everyone else: plain Astra

▹ the edge

alone each agent is mid. together they're a loop: find → prove → break → fix, and you rerun it on every new model

OpenAI own line: a low-privilege account on an unpatched box = root for a well-funded attacker. bot, hot wallet or validator key on a linux server you haven't updated? that's your threat model now

10 days after the scan: 61 fixes upstream · 43 staging · 299 discussed in public. the patch race already started

will models fix the internet faster than they break it?

I still don't understand why everyone is not using this yet. Thanks to it, a year ago I increased my income to 15,000 dollars a month

Andrey Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI, published a simple idea that got 25 million views: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain

You point Claude Code to a folder, drop any source in there (an article, transcript, PDF) and Claude reads it, links it, and saves it into a living wiki of everything you know. It compounds like interest: the more you feed it, the smarter it gets

Here is the gist:

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary:
At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra. [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] The piece was divided into three movements. The first movement, “SMASH UP,” was, in Machover’s words, a “clash/crisis” without audible enhancement from the AI.

The second, “WAKE UP,” was an “awakening”: the AI slowly produced sound in response to various solo lines in the orchestra. Then the last movement, “STAND UP,” was a “depiction of democracy,” as the musicians and AI listened to one another and negotiated the final musical product.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 is out. Here's what it actually changes for you if you build, research, or ship with AI.
items.summary:
Claude Fable 5.2 is out. Here's what it actually changes for you if you build, research, or ship with AI.

Skip the hype. The user view 👇

What it is
- Anthropic's top model, released Nov 9
- Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are the same model. Fable: all paid Claude plans + the API. Mythos: vetted cyber and life-sciences orgs
- $8 in / $40 out per 1M tokens, down from $10 / $50 on Fable 5.1
- Up to 30% faster output than 5.1. Optional fast mode: up to 2.5x faster at $16 / $80
- 1M context, 128K max output

If you write code
- FrontierSWE v2: 69.9% (Fable 5.1: 56.3%, Opus 5.5: 62.3%)
- FrontierCode 2.0, "would maintainers merge this?": 49.1%, the highest of any released model Anthropic tested
- On High effort it roughly matches Opus 5.5's best FrontierCode score for about half the cost per task
- Anthropic says agents on an earlier version moved a production service from Python to Rust. It now starts about 26x faster

If you do research or math
- About 1,000 Fable agents formalized Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean in 30 hours. Opus 5.5 with the same setup: 26% done at 18 hours
- Humanity's Last Exam (with tools): 74.2% vs 67.7% for Opus 5.5
- Solved two open black-hole physics problems (preprints, not yet peer reviewed)

If you're an analyst or run ops
- Remote Labor Index: 41.3%, up from 17.9% on Fable 5.1
- AutomationBench (business workflows): 51.4%, up from 31.4%. Gemini 4 Carbon still leads here at 53.9%
- Chart reading (Chartography): 73.4%, up from 44.8%
- Testers say it caught regional numbers that didn't sum to a 10-K total, and salary deposits that didn't match a bank balance

Independent check
- Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: #1 at 65 (max effort), ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon at 60 and Opus 5.5 at 59

The catch
- Per token it's still 2x Opus 5.5 ($4 / $20)
- Max effort gets expensive: $26.54 per task on Artificial Analysis vs $9.08 on High, which scores 62
- Safeguards block most cybersecurity work on Fable (about 55% fewer blocks than 5.1, Anthropic says)
- Some heavy users call it a "hall monitor"
- API needs 30-day data retention

Who should use it
- Hard, long, ambiguous work: big refactors, migrations, research, multi-agent runs. Start on High
- Everyday coding and chat: Anthropic itself says start with Opus 5.5
- A pattern people are trying: Fable plans, Opus or Sonnet executes

One prompt tip from Anthropic's guide: tell it "This codebase is yours: what it's for and how it's built are your call, and you'll keep building on it." It merged repeated code in about half of tries with that line, under a tenth without.

My take: don't default to Max. Run High, measure, and save Fable for work where a wrong answer costs more than the tokens.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python tính số Fibonacci bằng đệ quy (recursion):

```python
def fibonacci(n):
    """Hàm tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy."""
    # Điều kiện dừng (Base case)
    if n <= 0:
        return 0
    elif n == 1:
        return 1
    
    # Bước đệ quy (Recursive step)
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
# In ra 10 số Fibonacci đầu tiên
for i in range(10):
    print(f"F({i}) = {fibonacci(i)}")
```

**Lưu ý:** Cách viết đệ quy này rất dễ hiểu nhưng có độ phức tạp thời gian là $O(2^n)$, nghĩa là sẽ rất chậm hoặc tràn bộ nhớ nếu bạn tính với các số $n$ lớn (ví dụ $n > 30$). Đối với các bài toán thực tế cần tính số Fibonacci lớn, người ta thường dùng phương pháp khử đệ quy (lặp) hoặc dùng Memoization (lưu lại kết quả đã tính).

items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio.
